title: Add --fallback-model so overload does not kill unattended runs
source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference — `--fallback-model sonnet,haiku`: automatic fallback when the primary model is overloaded, comma-separated list tried in order
description: Every delegation (delegate.py:2697), Prometheus scan/evolve call (prometheus.py:393/415) and orchestrate plan call (orchestrate.py:843) pins a single --model. When Opus is overloaded the subprocess dies and the ticket lands in 'interrupted' / the sleepy iteration burns as a no-op — the failure mode behind several of the self-diagnosed proposals in the backlog. The CLI now supports an ordered fallback chain, which converts a hard failure into a silent, cheaper completion. This is the single lowest-effort durability win available for long unattended sleepy and Prometheus runs.
proposed_changes: 1) Add a FALLBACK_CHAINS dict in delegate.py mapping primary alias -> fallback list (opus -> 'sonnet', sonnet -> 'haiku', haiku -> none), overridable via env CTO_FALLBACK_MODELS. 2) In delegate_to_agent(), right after `cmd.extend(["--model", _resolve_model_for_cli(model)])`, add `cmd.extend(["--fallback-model", chain])` when the chain is non-empty and a capability probe confirms the flag exists. 3) Do the same for prometheus.py:393 and :415 and orchestrate.py:843. 4) Detect actual fallback in the stream-json 'result'/'system' events (the reported model differs from the requested one) and record `model_used` on the ticket plus a roro event so cost accounting in _last_stream_usage stays truthful about which model actually ran. 5) Skip the flag for reviewer-morty gates where a weaker model would undermine the two-gate review (PROM-174) — keep those strict-fail.
